hypothesis: The existing bounded triangle/diamond compaction transformation is unchanged. Its independently vectorized consumer can legitimately use the latch participant-count merge instead of the single-input LCSSA export when SCEV expands its trip count. Proving that limited SSA relationship repairs false-negative EVL and execution-checker expectations while strengthening rejection of consumers controlled by the original trip count or unrelated values. No new program legality, profitability, vectorizability or numerical prerequisites are introduced.
semantics: ScalarReductionFission.cpp builds a zero-start participant counter, advances it once on the common participating arm, and merges unchanged/advanced values at the unique producer latch. Before original iteration i, 0<=count<=i; each participating store indexes count<N<=M. The final P<=N fits the existing checked IV and full-trip scratch bound. The guard has only the producer latch as predecessor; its fission.participating.count PHI has exactly one incoming [fission.participating.merge, latch]. Thus both values denote P on every consumer invocation. The producer latch dominates the guard and every path to the vector preheader. Using its merge as the AVL initial incoming value on the vector.ph edge is dominance-correct. ScalarEvolution::createNodeForPHI simplifies a single-input PHI before taking its SCEV, and VPlanTransforms::addExplicitVectorLength initializes AVL from Plan.getTripCount(). The frozen failure therefore demonstrates legitimate forwarding, not a compiler defect. The repaired EVL checks tie the exact latch merge to the guard export and AVL seed, tie all three VP loads and both ordered FP reductions to the same EVL, and require AVL -= EVL until zero. Both integer result exports and both FP result exports must select their unchanged original starts on the empty edge and the actual reduction results on the nonempty edge. The execution checker now checks counter initialization, update/bypass PHI inputs, a once-per-participant increment, and the single-input export before accepting precisely merge or export in actual consumer control operands. For scalar-remainder consumers it checks the minimum-iteration bound, rounding input, rounded bound, tail-bypass comparison and scalar termination; for EVL it checks the AVL seed, active-length computation, VP load/ordered-reduction lengths and AVL decrement. Branch checks require those count predicates to control the actual vector/tail paths. It also checks the empty comparison/branch and every original accumulator start at the result join. This fixture parser supplements LLVM DOM/LI/SE verification and executable comparisons, rather than trying to prove arbitrary IR. Existing strict FP ordering, original producer branches/operations, inactive operands, scratch sharing, alias behavior, nested scratch reuse, masks, tails and live-outs remain under the previous transformation contract. Strictfp/constrained FP and unsafe effects/calls stay rejected; enabling the separate fission FP option does not reorder these early-path reductions.
costs: Let M be the proven maximum original trip count, P the participating count, and S the sum of allocation sizes of distinct contribution SSA values. Scratch capacity remains M*S plus existing ABI alignment padding, checked with unsigned overflow/index bounds and the existing 65536-byte default per-candidate ceiling. It does not shrink with P, is allocated statically in function entry, and can occupy frame space even on guarded bypass. Logical scratch traffic is P*S stores plus P*S loads, with no per-iteration mask/index arrays. The two mixed fixtures have four accumulators but one 65*i32, one 65*double and one 65*float array: 1044 accounted bytes including 4 padding bytes, and 32*P traffic bytes. The two i64 sums share one slot: 520 bytes and 16*P traffic. Nested i32/double uses 784 accounted bytes including 4 padding bytes, reused each row, and 24*sum(P_row) logical traffic; capacity does not multiply by Rows. Default-limit tests admit 16384 i32 slots (65536 bytes) and reject 16385 (65540); i8 capacity 255 is representable while 256 original trips are rejected. Real frame padding/cache traffic are not measured. Original input loads/helper calls execute once on their original branches, with zero new original-input rereads, contribution recomputation or duplicated producer operations. Counter overhead is one carried index PHI and latch merge per original iteration plus one nuw increment per participant, using existing producer control with no new per-iteration branch. Added consumer control runs P iterations, plus one zero-count guard per producer completion, a consumer preheader, dedicated loop exit and initial/result join. Normal LV may add its own independent vector/tail guards. There are no new alias/SCEV guards, full-trip masks, dynamic/unbounded allocations, general compaction machinery or profitability model. Analysis is linear in instructions/uses plus fixed CFG checks and existing SCEV analysis; emission uses distinct-contribution/export maps and the existing full-function dominator recalculation. Host-only probes perturb the test executable and are excluded from RVV codegen inputs. This repair changes no compiler emission or runtime costs. It adds only a small fixture-specific provenance check over printed SSA definitions/control operands and parser fixtures; there is no recursive equivalence solver, new guard, scratch allocation, reread, duplication, recomputation, storage machinery or profitability model.
limitations: No compiler, build, test runner, executable checker or try.sh was invoked by this worker. Only source/diff and whitespace review was performed. The frozen t000007 build compiled successfully but its first compact EVL RUN failed two AVL-name expectations; 36 of 37 mandatory lit files passed historically. Later RUN lines in that failing file, VectorizeTests, the full transformed host executable matrix and the 234 primary corpus compilations were not completed for that snapshot. All remain pending on this repaired snapshot; no fresh pass result or remaining failure list can yet be established. No compiler defect was exposed by the inspected evidence, so no compiler code changed. The parser recognizes the existing i64 compact-counter fixtures and only the demonstrated direct export/latch forwarding forms; arbitrary PHI/copy/arithmetic equivalences are deliberately unsupported. The parser-only synthetic suffixes are not semantic execution tests. Actual transformed-path execution still uses the unchanged scalar-compact.ll fixtures and C harness. Fixed-vscale host execution of the explicit scalar-remainder variant is not RVV target execution. Default EVL/VP receives IR and RVV machine-code verification only; host specialization still rejects those intrinsics. No RVV hardware/emulator execution or measured speedup is claimed. Transformation limits remain one bounded canonical triangle/diamond with a common participation stream and final add-reduction exports. Larger CFGs, differing streams, mixed/non-add recurrences, partial-state exports, effects/unsafe calls and strict/constrained FP remain unsupported. Scratch capacity remains full-trip and bounded per candidate, not tiled or capped across the whole function. No benchmark edits or additional fast-math/errno assumptions were made.

It rejects missing, inverted, nonzero, wrong-bound or wrong-condition empty guards, changed empty-path starts, wrong/multiple export inputs/edges, nonzero counter initialization, broken recurrence/bypass linkage and incorrect increments. Existing probe-placement checks remain and the compact parser fixture now models the actual count recurrence and control.
